rationale_evidence.anchor: "no document says X" is the weak evidence class, downgraded twice in the programme's history when fuller reading recovered what sampling had missed. The one absence promoted to a finding — the corpus's lack of any ratified decision — earned it by systematic search, not by sampling.
rationale_evidence.statement: Absence-claims ('no document says X') are treated as the weakest evidence class; the programme downgraded two such absence-claims after fuller reading recovered material that sampling had missed. The single absence-claim promoted to a genuine finding (the corpus's lack of any ratified decision) earned that status specifically because it rested on systematic search rather than sampling.

rationale_evidence.anchor: the corpus's most confident documents are its least reliable; its best results (EXP-01, the Step-050 audit) are the ones that state their own limits. The grading system is the corpus's hardest-won lesson, institutionalized.
rationale_evidence.statement: Justifies the whole grading apparatus by an empirical pattern found in the corpus itself: the most confident-sounding documents proved least reliable, while the most reliable results (EXP-01, the Step-050 audit) were exactly the ones that stated their own limits -- so the grading system institutionalizes the corpus's own hardest-won lesson.

rationale_evidence.anchor: No silent upgrade -- no sentence may raise the epistemic status of the evidence beneath it. Origin: standing rule of the book plan; enforced twice by independent review against this very book (a grade census that dropped a TESTED mark; two phrasings a notch above support -- both corrected under authorization, both preserved in the record). ... The echo rule -- the programme's own outputs, found saved back into the corpus, carry zero evidential weight.
rationale_evidence.statement: Enumerates six honesty rules each tied to a documented originating incident: the final rule (strongest statement never exceeds available evidence); no-silent-upgrade (caught twice by independent review against this book itself: a dropped TESTED mark, two overstated phrasings, both corrected); the echo rule (a saved status report was found inside the 'read-only' corpus, which an ungoverned reconstruction would have cited as self-confirming); dated statistics (the corpus grew while being studied, so an undated census becomes wrong); the verbatim rule (a ratified-wording column was found silently altered, caught by independent review); and claim-strength inheritance (added this Part after finding every post-correction defect lived in synoptic/compressed material).

- **[ARGUMENT]** [S1194]: Justifies the whole grading apparatus by an empirical pattern found in the corpus itself: the most confident-sounding documents proved least reliable, while the most reliable results (EXP-01, the Step-050 audit) were exactly the ones that stated their own limits -- so the grading system institutionalizes the corpus's own hardest-won lesson.
